summary: China's exports jump 35% and its surplus passes $1 trillion again, while Double 11 shoppers buy AI tools and want more than discounts.
body: China's customs agency said on Tuesday that October exports were 35.2% higher than a year ago, pushing the trade surplus for January to October to $1.04 trillion, the second year above $1 trillion, AP reports.[^1] Semiconductor exports more than doubled in value (up 137%) and car exports rose 37.6%, as the world's AI building boom pulls in Chinese electronics.[^1] Economists say the other side of this is weak spending at home: Alicia García-Herrero of Natixis says overcapacity and high savings keep China exporting and calls it "not sustainable".[^1] Trade will be a main topic when Trump and Xi meet at APEC in Shenzhen next week.[^1]

Daily life shows up in Double 11 (Nov 11), the biggest online shopping festival, now in its 18th year. This year's surprise best-seller is AI: a famous livestream host sold about 100,000 monthly plans for Alibaba's office AI assistant in 30 minutes, and Taobao and Tmall say token sales, paid units of AI use, rose 450% from the previous month on the first sale day, the Seoul Economic Daily reports, citing China's The Paper.[^2] Overall, spending across big platforms from Oct 7 to 31 was up only 2.4% from a year earlier, by data firm Syntun's count.[^2]

A survey cited in the same report found about 70% of shoppers say the festival loses its appeal if it only offers price cuts.[^2] My read: Chinese shoppers seem to be buying fewer things on impulse and more things they think will be useful, which fits the cautious mood seen in housing and car sales this year.

sources.title: China's trade surplus surpasses $1 trillion for a 2nd straight year, as exports surge 35%
